render_params.alt_text: HD 189733 b, Gas giant, 1.13 Jupiter radii (measured), colour family from the equilibrium temperature, lit by its star. Surface relief: illustrative.

confidence.formula: C = sum(w_i c_i) / sum(w_i): c is 1 for a measured value or a formula of measured values, a placeholder share for a model-dependent one, and 0 for an assumed, artistic or missing one; the w_i are placeholder weights (D-36, Q-221)
confidence.found: Data for: Radius, mass, orbit and tides, temperature and colour.
confidence.note: This is how much of the picture rests on data. It is not the probability that the picture is correct.
confidence.weights_note: Placeholder weights: they come from the approved prototype until a sensitivity sweep replaces them (D-36).

layers.description: Number of bands from the typical spin of a giant planet and the radius (Rhines scale, A7.2): about 24 from pole to pole. The jet speed is a typical value; the exact band pattern is a seeded look.
layers.formula: bands ~ sqrt(2 Omega R / U), Omega = 2 pi / P (Rhines scale, order of magnitude only)

layers.description: Flattening of the poles from the typical spin of a giant planet, with the mean density of Jupiter assumed (A7.2).
layers.formula: f = f_J (P_J / P)^2, from f = 0.7 q with q proportional to Omega^2

layers.description: Colour family chosen by the equilibrium temperature (A7.2).
layers.formula: palette family chosen by teq_K between the stops 60, 100, 130, 200, 600, 1100, 1800 K

layers.description: A few storms between the jets, as on the giant planets of the Solar System. How many and where is a seeded look; no measurement of this planet's storms is used.
Swirling detail along the band edges. Look only.

rgb.source: neutral stand-in swatch (R7.7); the drawn palette is the colour layer (A7.2)
